**Galois Group**

Let's start with the Galois group, denoted by G, which is a group of automorphisms of a field extension L/K. An automorphism is a bijective homomorphism from L to itself. The Galois group is the set of all automorphisms of L that fix K pointwise.

**Group Operation**

The group operation on G is function composition, denoted by ∘. For two automorphisms σ and τ in G, the composition σ ∘ τ is defined as (σ ∘ τ)(x) = σ(τ(x)) for all x in L.

**Order of the Galois Group**

The order of G, denoted by |G|, is the number of elements in G. It is also the degree of the field extension L/K, denoted by [L:K].

**Cyclic Subgroups**

A cyclic subgroup of G is a subgroup generated by a single element σ, denoted by <σ>. The order of <σ> is the smallest positive integer n such that σ^n = id, where id is the identity automorphism.

**Normal Subgroups**

A normal subgroup of G is a subgroup H such that σH = Hσ for all σ in G. The normal subgroups of G are the kernels of the irreducible representations of G.

**Irreducible Representations**

An irreducible representation of G is a representation that has no proper subrepresentations. The irreducible representations of G are the representations that are one-dimensional and have a trivial kernel.

A Galois invariant is a polynomial in L that is invariant under the action of G. In other words, if σ is an automorphism in G, then σ(f(x)) = f(x) for all x in L.

The Galois Invariant Theorem states that if f(x) is a polynomial in L that is invariant under the action of G, then f(x) is a polynomial in K[x] that is invariant under the action of G.

A splitting field of a polynomial f(x) in K[x] is a field extension L/K such that f(x) splits into linear factors in L[x].

A Galois extension is a field extension L/K that is a splitting field of some polynomial f(x) in K[x]. The Galois extension is a Galois extension if and only if the Galois group G is a finite group.

The Fundamental Theorem of Galois Theory states that there is a one-to-one correspondence between the subfields of L/K and the subgroups of G.
